caption: The button on a garage door remote is pressed, and the garage light comes on and the door begins to rise.

sa.check: A garage with its door closed and a remote in view.
The light is off and the door still before the press.
The order is press, then light and door together.

pc.expect: The light comes on and the door starts to rise together, right after the press, and only then.
pc.fail: The button is pressed and neither light nor door responds to the end of the clip; or the door rises while the light stays dark; or the light comes on while the door stays shut to the end; or the door begins to move before the button is pressed.

pc.expect: The door is still before the press and moves only after it, rising steadily in one direction.
pc.fail: The door rises before the press; or stops and starts with nothing pressed; or rises and drops back; or rattles in place without rising.

pc.expect: The door rises along its tracks as one panel or as hinged sections following each other, its bottom edge lifting off the ground.
pc.fail: The door swings outward like a gate while its tracks show a roll-up door; or the sections separate; or the door rises faster at one side so it tilts; or the door lifts as a whole off its tracks.

pc.expect: The light lights the garage: the floor and walls inside brighten from the fixture.
pc.fail: The fixture glows while the garage stays as dark as before; or the garage brightens while the fixture stays dark; or the light comes from a place other than the fixture.

pc.expect: One door in its frame; the door passes through nothing and stays attached; the light fixture stays on the ceiling.
pc.fail: The door passes through its frame or the ceiling; or a second door appears; or the door vanishes; or the fixture drops or vanishes.

pc.expect: The door's colour and panelling, the remote and the garage contents stay the same apart from the light.
pc.fail: The door changes colour or panel pattern; or the remote changes shape; or the garage contents rearrange.
